desc:
Once called "unreasonable" in Toshiro Kageyama's famous book Lessons in the Fundamentals of Go, we now regard this move as the best move for the local position. (The old joseki doesn't profit enough for White.) Blocking here leads to difficult fighting. The sequences that flow from this move have placed it among the most difficult joseki in existence, together with the avalanche, dagger, magic sword, and taisha.

If difficult fighting is unsavory, another move besides Q15 is recommended.
